prerequisites: Operating with concepts from fundamental disciplines
Assimilated and applied basic principles from physics (mechanics, thermodynamics, heat transfer)
General knowledge of applied chemistry (oxidation reactions, fuel composition)
Interpreting and creating functional drawings and diagrams
Applying mathematical calculation methods to solve engineering problems
Correlating physical phenomena with technical applications
Respecting safety and environmental protection norms in engineering activities

learning_outcomes.text: Explain the fundamental principles of thermodynamic cycles used in internal combustion engines (ICE), including ideal and real cycles (Otto, Diesel, etc.).
Describe and analyze the thermogasdynamic processes occurring in the engine cylinder: intake, compression, combustion, expansion, exhaust.
Identify and interpret the functional characteristics of internal combustion engines (torque, power, specific consumption, thermal efficiency curves).
Know the general constructive principles of thermal engines: types of configurations, main components, materials used, design criteria.
Understand the influence of operating parameters on the performance and emissions of internal combustion engines.
Apply thermodynamic and physicochemical concepts for the analysis/modeling of ICE operating cycles.
Calculate engine performance parameters (power, torque, specific consumption, hourly consumption, efficiency) based on experimental or theoretical data.
Interpret and correlate engine characteristic curves with the operating regime and practical application.
Utilize calculation and simulation tools for the study of internal engine processes (e.g., p-V diagrams, thermodynamic simulation, constructive solutions etc.).
Develop comparative analyses between different types of cycles and constructive configurations, depending on the application and technical requirements.
Have the ability to work autonomously in solving engineering problems related to the operation of piston thermal engines.
Demonstrate responsibility in using knowledge to evaluate the energy and ecological impact of propulsion systems.
Have a proactive attitude in identifying technical solutions for optimizing engine performance and reducing emissions.
Have the ability to communicate technical analysis results efficiently, both orally and in writing, using specific terminology for the field.
Demonstrate openness to continuous learning and the integration of new technologies in the field of thermal propulsion.
Develop professional projects in the field of engineering.

syllabus_topics: Introductory notions. Definitions. Classification of piston internal combustion engines. History of piston engine development, in relation to the technical-economic evolution of society. Utilities provided by thermal engines. Representative achievements.
Indicated and effective parameters of internal combustion engines for road vehicles. Indicated parameters. Effective parameters. General factors influencing combustion in spark ignition engines.
Operating regimes of internal combustion engines. Defining the load of internal combustion engines for road vehicles. Particularities of spark ignition engines and compression ignition engines.

Theoretical cycles of piston internal combustion engines. Basic hypotheses for the thermodynamic study of cycles. General theoretical cycle of internal combustion engines. Usual theoretical cycles of piston internal combustion engines. Analysis of the mixed theoretical cycle. Particularities of the mixed theoretical cycle. Theoretical cycle of spark ignition engines. Theoretical cycle of compression ignition engines with slow operating regime.

Influences on the thermal efficiency of theoretical cycles. Influences on the thermal efficiency of the theoretical cycle of spark ignition engines. Influences on the thermal efficiency of the theoretical cycle of compression ignition engines with slow operating regime. Influences on the thermal efficiency of the theoretical cycle of compression ignition engines with rapid operating regime. Comparisons between usual theoretical cycles of piston internal combustion engines.

Normal intake in four-stroke engines. Criteria for assessing the efficiency of the intake process. Influences on normal intake in four-stroke engines. Influence of fresh charge properties. Influence of functional factors. Influence of constructive factors. Determination of specific parameters of the intake process. Pressure in the cylinder at the end of the intake stroke. Increase in fresh fluid temperature. Temperature at the end of the intake stroke. Filling degree.

Study of the exhaust process in four-stroke engines. Criteria for the perfection of the exhaust process. Analysis of the exhaust process using the indicated diagram. Determination of the exhaust valve opening moment. Determination of the exhaust valve closing moment. Pressure and temperature of gases at the end of exhaust. Exhaust adjustment settings. Influences on the exhaust process.
Study of compression and expansion processes of four-stroke internal combustion engines. Study of the compression process. Study of the expansion process.

Study of the combustion process in four-stroke engines. Premises of ignition and combustion in spark ignition engines. Staging of normal combustion in spark ignition engines. General factors influencing combustion in spark ignition engines. Characteristic aspects of combustion in spark ignition engines. Optimization of the compression ratio in spark ignition engines. Abnormal combustion phenomena in spark ignition engines. Influence of combustion chamber type and architecture on the combustion process in spark ignition engines. Particularities of combustion in compression ignition engines. Analysis of combustion in compression ignition engines using the indicated diagram. Notions of combustion thermodynamics.

Two-stroke piston internal combustion engines. Conceptual-functional aspects. Realization solutions. Functional cycles. Indicated and developed diagrams of the two-stroke cycle for naturally aspirated and supercharged engines. Comparison between two-stroke and four-stroke engines. Specific areas of use for two-stroke piston internal combustion engines.

Supercharging of piston internal combustion engines. Solutions for supercharging. Classifications. Characteristics. Turbo-supercharging. Compressor. Turbine. Turbocharger bearings. Control of turbo-supercharging pressure. Variable geometry turbocharger. Engine start and stop. Intercooler. Reduction of pollution. EGR system.

Regulation characteristics. Regulation characteristic based on hourly fuel consumption. Regulation characteristic based on spark advance. Regulation characteristic based on injection advance. Detonation characteristic. Dosage characteristic. Functional characteristics. Load characteristic. Speed characteristic. Speed characteristic at total load and full load. Speed characteristic at partial loads. Speed characteristic at zero load. Loss characteristic.

Propulsion characteristics. Complex characteristics. Correction of characteristics. Traction qualities of automotive engines. Relative speed characteristic. Engine testing. Organization of the test bench for engines. Engine equipping for testing. Organization of the test bench for engines. Engine equipping for testing.

Notions of piston internal combustion engine construction. Conceptual and constructive particularities of high-power internal combustion engines. Conceptual and constructive particularities of medium-power internal combustion engines. Conceptual and constructive particularities of small-displacement internal combustion engines. Selection of dimensional parameters (stroke, bore, compression ratio, etc.). Establishment of the constructive-functional formula (number of strokes of the engine cycle; number of cylinders and their arrangement; choice of ignition solution, etc.).
Labor safety norms specific to the ICE laboratory. Presentation of the main energy solutions specific to internal combustion engines for road vehicles.
Experimental determination of the real cycle distribution phases in four-stroke engines and interpretation of results.
Experimental determination of the filling coefficient in internal combustion engines.
Experimental plotting of the idle characteristic. Analytical plotting of the speed characteristic at total (external) load.
Construction of the engine mechanism. Constructive solutions for piston realization.
Construction of the gas distribution mechanism in four-stroke piston internal combustion engines.
Establishment of the engine's constructive-functional formula.
Analytical plotting of the indicated diagram (p-V coordinates). Plotting of the developed diagram (p-u coordinates).
Determination of the indicated and effective parameters of the engine.
Determination of piston stroke variation as a function of crank angle. Briks diagram.
Determination of piston speed and acceleration variation as a function of crank angle.
Constructive solutions for supercharging. Construction of the supercharging turbocharger.
Catch-up session for laboratory work.
Balance session.
assessment_rules: The final evaluation result for a discipline is obtained by considering the scores and weights allocated to each activity within the discipline. Whole grades from 10 to 1 will be awarded. A grade of 5 certifies the acquisition of the minimal learning outcomes for a discipline and the awarding of its corresponding study credits.
